Conditions and time limits:

To claim compensation in a hit-and-run motor accident where the identity of the vehicle cannot be ascertained, an application for compensation can be made under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, as applied by Section 161 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 [1][2]. 

- The application may be made by all or any of the legal representatives of the deceased, or by any agent duly authorised by them, as provided under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 [2].
- Where all the legal representatives of the deceased have not joined in the application, it shall be made on behalf of or for the benefit of all of them, and the ones who have not joined shall be impleaded as respondents, under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 [2].
- The application shall be made, at the option of the claimant, either to the Claims Tribunal having jurisdiction over the area in which the accident occurred, or to the Claims Tribunal within the local limits of whose jurisdiction the claimant resides or carries on business, or within the local limits of whose jurisdiction the defendant resides, pursuant to Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 [2].

rows.answer:
The punishment for a first offence of driving by a drunken person or by a person under the influence of drugs is imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or a fine which may extend to two thousand rupees, or both, under Section 185 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 [1][3]. For a second or subsequent offence, it is punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to three thousand rupees, or with both, under Section 185 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 [1][3]. In Madhya Pradesh, under Section 185 of the Madhya Pradesh Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1991, the punishment for the first offence is imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with a fine of ten thousand rupees, or with both, and for a second or subsequent offence with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with a fine of fifteen thousand rupees, or with both [4].

Related provisions:
- Section 203 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, which covers breath tests and the procedure for requiring specimens of breath from drivers [8].

No petition for divorce can be presented to the court unless one year has elapsed since the date of the marriage, as provided under Section 14 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 [1], and Section 29 of the Special Marriage Act, 1954 [3]. 

Conditions and time limits:
- One year must have elapsed from the date of the marriage (or the date of entering the certificate of marriage in the Marriage Certificate Book under the Special Marriage Act, 1954) before presenting a petition for divorce [1][3].
- The court may allow a petition to be presented before one year has elapsed if the case is one of exceptional hardship to the petitioner or of exceptional depravity on the part of the respondent, upon an application made in accordance with the rules [1][3].
- When disposing of such an application, the court must have regard to the interests of any children of the marriage and to whether there is a reasonable probability of reconciliation between the parties before the expiration of the one year [1][3].

Phone churane ki saza (theft ke liye punishment) yeh hai ki chor ko kisi bhi tarah ki qaid (imprisonment) di ja sakti hai jo teen saal tak ho sakti hai, ya jurmana (fine), ya dono ho sakte hain, aur agar kisi ko is section ke tahat dusri baar ya uske baad doshi thahraya jata hai, toh use kathor karavas (rigorous imprisonment) hoga jo ek saal se kam ka nahi hoga lekin paanch saal tak ka ho sakta hai, aur saath hi jurmana bhi hoga [1]. Yeh current law Section 303 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 ke antargat hai, jo ki pehle ke Indian Penal Code ke Section 379 ko replace kar chuka hai [1][8].

Conditions and time limits:
- Agar chori ki gayi property ki keemat paanch hazaar rupaye se kam hai aur koi vyakti pehli baar doshi thahraya gaya hai, toh property ki keemat lautane ya chori ki gayi property ko wapas karne par use community service ki saza di jayegi [1].

rows.answer:
Section 379 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 has been replaced by Section 303 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which is the current law [1][6]. 

The punishment for theft is imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both, and for a second or subsequent conviction, rigorous imprisonment for a term of not less than one year and up to five years with fine, with a proviso that a first-time offender where the stolen property is valued at less than five thousand rupees shall be punished with community service upon return or restoration of the property [1]. (This replaces previously Section 379 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 [6].)

Conditions and time limits:
- The offence requires an intention to take movable property dishonestly out of the possession of any person without consent by moving that property [1].
- For first-time offenders where the stolen property's value is less than five thousand rupees, community service applies upon return of the value of the property or restoration of the stolen property [1].

The old law this replaced: section 378 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (Theft) [7].

rows.answer:
In Miranda v. Arizona, the US Supreme Court considered whether an accused must be apprised of the right not to answer and keep silent while being interrogated by the police, and observed that if a person in custody is to be subjected to interrogation, that person must first be informed in clear and unequivocal terms of the right to remain silent [12]. The US Supreme Court held that the prosecution may not use statements, whether exculpatory or inculpatory, stemming from custodial interrogation of the defendant unless it demonstrates the use of procedural safeguards effective to secure the privilege against self-incrimination [11].

Conditions and time limits:
- The warning of the right to remain silent must be given at the outset, as an absolute prerequisite in overcoming the inherent pressures of the interrogation atmosphere [12].
